name: Same lines changed differently
rule: Both sides changed the same base lines and their texts differ, so a line-based merge reports a conflict, even if part of the change is identical.
example: Left renames a function in an import line; right renames it too and also changes the import path on that line.

name: Reformatting misaligns tokens
rule: One side reformatted code (line breaks, indentation) that the other side edited, and the separator-based alignment pairs fragments that differ only in layout or are shifted, so the tool conflicts.
example: Right splits an import list over several lines; the conflict block pairs left's `createTheme` with right's `createTheme,` and the next item.

name: Resolved structurally
rule: The sides' edits are identical or touch different syntax-tree nodes, so the structured merge combines them without conflict.
example: Both sides rename the same imported identifier, and only one side also changes the import path; the tool keeps both.

name: Reprints layout
rule: The output differs from the merge commit only in layout, because the tool reprints the merged code in its own formatting.
example: A multi-line import list comes out on one line, and the final newline is dropped.

name: Compatible at syntax level
rule: A conflicts on textual overlap, but the sides' changes don't conflict at the syntax level (identical changes, or changes to different elements), so B merges them and matches the merge commit by design.
example: Both sides rename the same import and one side also reformats it; A conflicts, B keeps the rename and the reformatting.
